intents.title: Split an amount by weights without losing a cent
intents.why: Gift splits and refunds divide one amount between several parties by weight.
acceptance: src/core/money.ts exports allocate(m: Money, weights: number[]): Money[]
The parts always sum exactly to m, in m's currency
Leftover cents go one each to the parts with the largest fractional remainders; ties go to the earlier part
Works for negative amounts the same way, mirrored
Throws a RangeError for an empty weights list, a negative weight, or weights that sum to zero

intents.title: Parse money strings strictly
intents.why: Imported price lists contain messy strings; bad ones must be rejected, not guessed.
acceptance: parse keeps its signature and accepts what it accepted before
parse also accepts a leading + sign and thousands separators in groups of exactly three digits: parse("1,234.50") is money(123450)
parse rejects with a SyntaxError: empty or whitespace-only strings, "1,23.00", "1,2345", ".5", "5.", "1e3", "--1", "1.234", and any string with inner spaces
parse("-0") and parse("-0.00") are money(0) with cents exactly 0, not -0
parseCatalog keeps working: a catalog price never contains a thousands separator, because the comma separates fields

intents.title: Format negative amounts in currencies without a symbol
intents.why: Reports in CHF and JPY print negative amounts wrongly today.
acceptance: format keeps its signature
For a currency with no symbol, a negative amount is written with the minus before the number: format(money(-1234, "CHF")) is "-12.34 CHF"
A currency named in a new exported MINOR_UNITS table with 0 minor units is written with no decimals: format(money(1234, "JPY")) is "1234 JPY" and format(money(-5, "JPY")) is "-5 JPY"
MINOR_UNITS lists at least JPY: 0 and KRW: 0; every other currency keeps two decimals
Existing USD, EUR and GBP output is unchanged

intents.title: Stack discounts with a cap
intents.why: Marketing wants a coupon and a loyalty discount on one order, but never more than half off.
acceptance: src/discount.ts exports stackDiscounts(subtotal: Money, discounts: Discount[]): Money, the total amount off
Percent discounts apply in order, each to what is left after the previous ones, rounded half away from zero at each step
Fixed discounts apply after every percent discount, in the order given
The total off never exceeds half of the subtotal, rounded down to a whole cent, and never makes the result negative
An empty list is zero off

intents.title: Tax-inclusive prices
intents.why: Some regions show prices with tax already included; invoices must split the tax back out.
acceptance: src/tax.ts exports taxIncluded(gross: Money, region: string): Money, the tax part of a gross price that already contains tax at the region's rate
net plus taxIncluded is exactly the gross; the tax is rounded half away from zero to a whole cent
taxIncluded(money(10725), "CA") is money(725)
A region with a zero rate gives zero; an unknown region throws a RangeError as taxFor does
taxIncluded(money(999), "TX") is money(59)

intents.title: Credit an invoice line by line
intents.why: Partial returns must credit only some lines, with the right share of discount, tax and shipping.
acceptance: src/credit.ts exports creditLines(invoice: Invoice, skus: string[]): Money, the amount to refund for returning every unit of those lines
The refund is those lines' totals, less their share of the invoice discount by line total, plus the tax on that discounted amount at the invoice's region rate
Shipping is refunded only when every line is returned
Returning every line refunds exactly the invoice total
An unknown sku throws a RangeError naming it

intents.title: Sales report across currencies
intents.why: The report throws for mixed currencies; finance wants one block per currency instead.
acceptance: salesReport keeps its signature and its exact output for invoices in one currency
For mixed currencies it writes one block per currency, in the order each currency first appears, each block its invoice lines then "TOTAL <currency> <sum>"
Blocks are separated by one empty line
An empty list gives "TOTAL 0.00"
The existing test that expects a TypeError for mixed currencies describes the old behavior: change it to the new one

intents.title: Merge carts
intents.why: A guest cart is merged into the account cart at sign-in.
acceptance: src/cart.ts exports mergeCarts(a: Cart, b: Cart): Cart
Lines for the same sku are combined into one line, at a's position, with the quantities added and a's product kept
Lines only in b are appended in b's order
Carts in different currencies throw a TypeError; neither input cart is changed
A merged quantity above 99 is capped at 99

intents.title: Shipping by weight band
intents.why: Flat shipping loses money on heavy orders.
acceptance: src/shipping.ts exports shippingByWeight(grams: number, region: string, currency?: string): Money
Up to and including 500 g costs the flat rate shippingFor gives; each started further 500 g adds 250 cents
0 grams is the flat rate; a negative or non-integer weight throws a RangeError
An unknown region throws as shippingFor does

intents.title: Tax is a cent short on some orders
intents.why: Customers in California report that tax on some orders is one cent less than their own calculation. Find and fix the cause in the money core.
acceptance: percentOf(money(200), 7.25) is money(15), and taxFor(money(3000), "CA") is money(218)
percentOf gives the exactly rounded result (halves away from zero) for every whole number of cents and every rate in TAX_RATES
percentOf keeps its signature and units: 15 still means 15 percent
A test in test/money.test.ts covers amounts that used to be a cent short

intents.title: Search the catalog
intents.why: The shop needs a search box over product names.
acceptance: src/catalog.ts exports searchCatalog(catalog: ReadonlyMap<string, Product>, query: string): Product[]
Matches are case-insensitive and ignore accents: "cafe" finds "Café"
Every word of the query must appear in the name, in any order
Results are sorted by how early the first query word appears in the folded name, then by the folded name (lower case, accents removed), then by sku
An empty or whitespace-only query returns an empty list

intents.title: Invoice totals that always add up
intents.why: Auditors found invoices whose line totals do not add up to the subtotal after discounts.
acceptance: Invoice gains discountedLines: Money[], one per line: each line total less its share of the discount
The discount shares are allocated by line total and always sum exactly to the invoice discount
Leftover cents go to the lines with the largest fractional remainders; ties go to the earlier line
Every other Invoice field and buildInvoice's signature are unchanged

intents.title: Parse CSV files correctly
intents.why: Price-list imports break on quoted fields.
acceptance: src/csv.ts exports parseCsv(text: string): string[][], one array of fields per record, following RFC 4180
Quoted fields may contain commas, newlines, and doubled quotes that mean one quote
Records end with LF or CRLF; a final line ending does not add an empty record; an empty input is []
Spaces are kept as they are; an empty line in the middle is a record with one empty field
Throws a SyntaxError for an unterminated quote, a quote inside an unquoted field, or text right after a closing quote

intents.title: Write amounts in words for checks
intents.why: Printed refund checks need the amount in words.
acceptance: src/words.ts exports toWords(m: Money): string for USD amounts
Format: "<dollars in words> dollar(s)" then " and <cents in words> cent(s)" only when cents are not zero; singular for exactly one
Numbers use lowercase English with hyphens for 21-99 and no "and" inside numbers: 115 is "one hundred fifteen"; scales up to millions
Zero dollars is "zero dollars"; negative amounts start with "minus "
Throws a RangeError for any currency other than USD or for more than 999,999,999.99 dollars

intents.title: Due dates in business days
intents.why: Invoices are due a number of business days after issue.
acceptance: src/dates.ts exports addBusinessDays(date: string, days: number, holidays?: string[]): string with YYYY-MM-DD dates in UTC
Saturdays, Sundays and the given holidays are not business days; negative days count backward
0 days returns the date itself when it is a business day, else the next business day
Throws a RangeError for a date that does not exist or is not YYYY-MM-DD, or for a non-integer number of days

intents.title: Pay in installments
intents.why: Checkout offers monthly payments with interest.
acceptance: src/installments.ts exports installments(total: Money, months: number, aprPercent: number): Array<{ payment, interest, principal, balance }> of Money
Monthly rate is apr/12; the standard payment is the annuity payment rounded half away from zero; with zero interest it is the total divided by months rounded down
Each month: interest is the balance times the monthly rate, rounded half away from zero; principal is payment minus interest; the last month pays the whole remaining balance plus its interest
Principals sum exactly to the total and the final balance is zero
Throws a RangeError for months that are not an integer from 1 to 360, a negative or non-finite rate, or a total that is not positive

intents.title: Match SKUs with glob patterns
acceptance: src/glob.ts exports matchSku(pattern: string, sku: string): boolean, matching the whole SKU
* matches any run of characters including none, ? exactly one, [abc] and ranges [a-z] one of a set, [!...] one not in the set
] right after [ or [! is a literal; - first or last in a set is a literal; an unclosed [ is a literal [
\\ makes the next character literal; a trailing backslash throws a SyntaxError
Matching must stay fast for patterns with many stars: no backtracking blow-up
